---
title: "Quiz · Engineering Through Stories"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. What is the foundational principle of this course?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
We do not simplify technology by abandoning its engineering model. We understand
the model first, transform it deliberately, and use story to make that
understanding accessible.
:::

## 2. Name the five stages of the architectural principle pipeline.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Technical Model, Metaphor, Story, Screenplay, Audio Producer (producing the
Audio Artifact).
:::

## 3. Which stage answers "WHAT IS TRUE?"

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The **Technical Model** stage. Its output is `concept.md`.
:::

## 4. Why does the course begin by having you listen to the finished story?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The course uses a reverse-engineering approach. You experience the result first,
then progressively learn how it was constructed. This mirrors the learning loop:
experience, deconstruct, construct, reflect.
:::

## 5. What happens if an error is found in the finished audio?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
You trace it back to its origin stage. A technical error belongs in the model, a
misleading analogy in the metaphor, confusing dialogue in the story, and a bad
pronunciation in rendering. Because every stage is inspectable, you fix the error
where it was introduced.
:::
